title: Final review of foundations epic diff
description: Review the integrated epic diff: bundle isolation from cloud/worker, auth soundness (derived hash, constant-time compare, rotation), deploy idempotency, setup secret-handling paths, schema codegen consistency across Go and TS.
notes:
2026-08-19 17:38 - FINAL REVIEW (frontier, read-only, controller checkout, git diff main...HEAD = 106 files, +10392/-88).

Reviewed against the tick's named axes plus correctness/security/test-quality/drift.

PASS — bundle isolation (D16): cloud/factory/test/isolation.test.ts asserts no src file imports outside the bundle, and that wrangler directives carry no ticks.sh domain, no tickboard assets, no shared D1, no routes. Nothing under cloud/worker/ was modified by the factory work.
PASS — auth soundness: salted PBKDF2 record, constant-time compare with a no-early-exit proof, middleware ahead of routing so 401/404 are indistinguishable, fail-closed 503 when unconfigured, per-request secret read so rotation needs no redeploy. Exempt policy is exactly /health plus the /api/hooks prefix with boundary matching. All verified live against the real edge, not only in workerd.
PASS — deploy idempotency: verified live — second and third runs reused the D1 database and R2 bucket, applied no migrations, and preserved the token.
PASS — setup secret handling: no write path targets the repo; credentials go to Worker secrets and ~/.ticksrc at 0600 only. tk factory status prints no secret material.
PASS — codegen consistency: make codegen-go + make codegen-ts produce a zero diff on the merged tree.
PASS — drift scan: no '|| true', suppressed errors, empty catch blocks, nolint/eslint-disable, --force, or HACK/XXX/TODO-remove markers in the added lines. No new go.mod dependencies.

FINDINGS

1. SHOULD-FIX (confidence high) — scripts/check-public-repo.mjs:107 hardcodes 'example.com' as the ONLY acceptable email domain. That forced xrk to rewrite pre-existing fixtures from '@example.invalid' to '@example.com' in internal/ (authority@, gate@, ticks-runner@, planning@, planning-death@). RFC 2606 reserves .invalid precisely so it can never resolve, which makes it strictly SAFER in fixtures than example.com — a real, routable domain. The guard drove a small correctness regression in code it was meant to protect. Fix: accept the RFC-reserved set (example.com/org/net, and the .invalid/.test/.localhost/.example TLDs) and revert those fixtures.

2. SHOULD-FIX (confidence high) — /health reports auth.configured from parseTokenHash alone, so a record that PARSES but cannot DERIVE still reports configured:true. This is not hypothetical: it is exactly the contradiction that made the 210k-iteration bug expensive to diagnose (health said configured while every authenticated request 503'd). t9k flagged it as out of scope, correctly. With the cap enforced in code and tests that combination should no longer arise, but a health check that actually exercises a derivation removes the whole class. Raised by the incident that this epic exists to close.

No blockers. Both findings are routed as repair ticks rather than deferred, per the no-silent-deferral rule.
